title: Componentwise scalar gluing for a nodal cluster ideal
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a nonempty projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at nodes, meaning that every singular closed point has completed local $k$-algebra $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $C$ be its finite set of irreducible components with their reduced structures [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $L$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $T\subset X$ be a zero-dimensional closed subscheme, possibly empty, with ideal $I_T$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $s\in H^0(X,I_T\otimes L)$ be nonzero at every component generic point [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Regard these sections as sections of $L$. Define $W_s$ to be the vector space of sections $t\in H^0(X,I_T\otimes L)$ such that $t|_\Gamma=a_\Gamma s|_\Gamma$ for a scalar $a_\Gamma\in k$ on every $\Gamma\in C$.
At each node $x$ joining distinct components $\Gamma,\Delta$, choose a local frame of $L$ and an ordering of the completed branches. Write $R_x=k[[u,v]]/(uv)\hookrightarrow k[[u]]\times k[[v]]$, $J_x=I_{T,x}R_x$, and write the completed germ of $s$ as $(f_x,g_x)\in J_x$. Call $x$ constrained if $(f_x,0)\notin J_x$, where membership includes membership in the equal-constant subring $R_x$. Then the coefficient map
$$W_s\longrightarrow k^C,\qquad t\longmapsto(a_\Gamma)_{\Gamma\in C}$$
is injective and has image exactly
$$\{a\in k^C:a_\Gamma=a_\Delta\text{ at every constrained node joining }\Gamma,\Delta\}.$$
The condition of being constrained is independent of the frame, branch ordering, and chosen nodal presentation. Self-nodes impose no condition on the single component coefficient. No reducedness, Cartier, or smooth-support condition on $T$, and no connectedness hypothesis on $X$, is required.

source.place: Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node), together with varieties.tex Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion) and algebra.tex Tag 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat). Agent-written coefficient-space consequence for an arbitrary ideal twist; supports Franciosi--Tenni Lemma 3.6(i), printed p.241.

proof.text: Projectivity implies properness, so the nodal normalization model makes $X$ Noetherian, with finitely many components and nodes. Put $F=I_T\otimes L$ and $E=\prod_{\Gamma\in C}i_{\Gamma,*}(L|_\Gamma)$, where $i_\Gamma:\Gamma\hookrightarrow X$. Restriction defines $F\to L\to E$. In a frame of $L$ at $x$, write $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and let $P_\Gamma$ be the stalk ideal of a component through $x$. The component-stalk calculus gives $E_x=\prod_{\Gamma\ni x}A/P_\Gamma$ and $\bigcap_{\Gamma\ni x}P_\Gamma=0$, since their reduced union is $X$. Here the stalk of a finite product is the product of stalks: choose representatives on a common intersection of finitely many neighbourhoods. Thus $A\to E_x$ is injective, and $F_x=I_{T,x}\subset A$ injects too. Exactness detected on stalks proves $F\hookrightarrow E$. All these identifications are in frames; changing frame multiplies every entry by the same unit.

source.place: Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node), nodal setup; modules.tex Tag 01AG (lemma-abelian); morphisms.tex Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper). Agent assembly using the cited component-stalk statements.

proof.text: For each component $\Gamma$, apply the nodal subcurve-boundary theorem with $Y=\Gamma$, $Z$ the reduced union of the other components, and $N=X$. A point on two distinct components lies in $Y\cap Z$ and is therefore a closed node. At a node the split-node component theorem gives exactly two possibilities: one minimal prime, equal to zero, or two minimal primes whose extended ideals in $R=\widehat A$ are $(u),(v)$. In the first case the two formal branches belong to the same component. Consequently, whenever only one component $\Gamma$ passes through $x$ (including a self-node), step 1 gives $E_x=A$. The coefficient tuple $q=(a_\Gamma s|_\Gamma)_\Gamma\in H^0(X,E)$ then has germ $a_\Gamma s_x\in I_{T,x}=F_x$ in a frame. No restriction on $a_\Gamma$ occurs there.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), statement (2) and proof, the distinction between one and two irreducible components through the point; Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node).

proof.text: Now let $x$ join distinct components, and put $I=I_{T,x}\subset A$. By the completed normalization model $A$ is Noetherian local of dimension one. Its map to $R=\widehat A$ is faithfully flat. Tensor the exact sequence $0\to I\to E_x\to E_x/I\to0$ with $R$; flat tensor exactness identifies the kernel of $E_x\otimes_A R\to(E_x/I)\otimes_A R$ with the image of $I\otimes_A R$. Faithful flat universal injectivity applied to the module $E_x/I$ shows that $q_x$ lies in $I$ if and only if $q_x\otimes1$ lies in that image. The split-node component theorem identifies $E_x\otimes_A R=(R/(v))\times(R/(u))=k[[u]]\times k[[v]]$, ordered according to the components. Under this identification the map $I\otimes_A R\to E_x\otimes_A R$ has image precisely $IR=J_x$ in the equal-constant subring: its elements are sums of products of images of elements of $I$ with elements of $R$. The completed tuple is $(a_\Gamma f_x,a_\Delta g_x)$. Thus local liftability into the full ideal is equivalent to membership of this pair in $J_x$.

source.place: Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node), with varieties.tex Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion); algebra.tex Tags 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat), 00HD (lemma-flat), 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective).

proof.text: In the product of branch rings abbreviate $J=J_x$, $(f,g)=(f_x,g_x)$ and $a=a_\Gamma$, $b=a_\Delta$. Since $(f,g)\in J$, the identity $(af,bg)=b(f,g)+(a-b)(f,0)$ gives $(af,bg)\in J$ if and only if $(a-b)(f,0)\in J$. If $(f,0)\in J$, every pair of scalars works. Otherwise this happens exactly when $a=b$: for $a-b\ne0$, multiplication by its inverse in $k$ would put $(f,0)$ in $J$. This calculation takes place in the product but tests membership in $J\subset R$; it therefore includes the equal-constant requirement, even when $(f,0)$ is not in $R$.

source.place: Agent linear-algebra calculation in the completed branch-ring model of Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node), retaining an arbitrary ideal rather than just the structure ring.

proof.text: For any tuple $a\in k^C$ satisfying the constrained-node equalities, form the section $q$ of $E$ from step 2. Steps 2--4 show that $q_x$ belongs to the image of $F_x$ at every point $x$. Stalk exactness identifies this image with the stalk of the image subsheaf. More explicitly, choose a preimage germ at $x$, represent it by a section of $F$ on a neighbourhood, and shrink until its image equals $q$. These local lifts agree on overlaps by the injection $F\hookrightarrow E$ in step 1, so the sheaf axiom glues them to a unique $t\in H^0(X,F)$ mapping to $q$. Its restrictions are the prescribed scalar multiples, hence $t\in W_s$. Conversely, if $t\in W_s$, its image in $E$ is this tuple, so its germs lie in $F_x$; steps 3--4 force equality of its two coefficients at every constrained node. This proves the asserted image exactly.

source.place: Agent assembly by the sheaf axiom from modules.tex Tag 01AG (lemma-abelian), stalk images and exactness, and the preceding completed local calculation.

proof.text: The coefficients of a section in $W_s$ are unique: evaluate $(a_\Gamma-b_\Gamma)s|_\Gamma=0$ at the component generic point, where $s$ is nonzero; a nonzero scalar acts invertibly, so $a_\Gamma=b_\Gamma$. The coefficient assignment is linear by addition and scalar multiplication of these restrictions. If its value is zero, every component restriction is zero, and the injection into $E$ in step 1 makes the section zero. It is thus the claimed injective linear map.

source.place: Agent linear-algebra consequence of generic nonvanishing and the restriction injection in step 1.

proof.text: Finally, the constrained condition is intrinsic to the local data. A frame change multiplies $(f,g)$ and its one-branch part by a unit of $R$; an ideal is stable under this unit and its inverse, so membership is unchanged. Swapping branches replaces $(f,0)$ by $(0,g)$, and $(0,g)=(f,g)-(f,0)$ gives equivalent membership. The split-node component theorem identifies the two branch rings canonically as the two quotients of $R$ by its minimal primes. An isomorphism between nodal presentations permutes these primes, induces the corresponding quotient isomorphisms, sends $J$ to its presented ideal and sends the projected pair to the corresponding projected pair (possibly swapped). Hence it preserves the same membership test. Step 2 already treats self-nodes with their single component coefficient. The proof used no condition on the finite subscheme beyond its ideal and no connectedness assumption; it applies also to $T=\varnothing$, to arbitrary nonreduced clusters, and component by component on a disconnected $X$.
